toml:
# Doppler-only positioning from a broadband constellation used as a signal of opportunity.
#
# The Starlink downlink carries no navigation message and its code and carrier phase are not
# usable for ranging, but its Doppler is: Kozhaya, Saroufim and Kassas ("Unveiling Starlink
# for PNT", NAVIGATION 72(1), 2025, https://navi.ion.org/content/72/1/navi.685) track the
# 240 MHz OFDM beacon at 11.325 GHz with a Doppler error of about 30 Hz (one sigma) and report
# about 2 m three-dimensional error in 20 s with three satellites. This scenario uses the
# `starlink-sop` preset: the first shell of 1584 satellites at 550 km and 53 deg (FCC 21-48;
# the Walker phasing is representative) with that Doppler error, a stationary receiver in
# Columbus, Ohio, a window of one minute, and one Doppler measurement per satellite every
# 0.1 s (the beacon repeats every 4/3 ms, so a receiver can form Doppler far faster; whether
# faster estimates are independent is not known, so the rate is a modelling input).
#
# The error-against-window table is the comparison with the published figure. It is a
# MODELLED consistency check, not a reproduction: the paper's receiver estimated the
# satellite states and oscillator offsets from real captures, while this model has a perfect
# ephemeris and puts every error into the 30 Hz Doppler sigma.
kind = "leo-pvt"
mode = "doppler"
seed = 11
duration_s = 60.0
step_s = 0.1

[user]
lat_deg = 40.0
lon_deg = -83.0
height_m = 220.0

[doppler]
# The receiver knows its height to 5 m (a barometer or a terrain model): Doppler from one
# shell at 53 deg constrains the vertical weakly over a short window.
height_sigma_m = 5.0
windows_s = [5.0, 10.0, 20.0, 40.0, 60.0]

[[system]]
name = "Starlink SoP"
leo_preset = "starlink-sop"
mask_deg = 25.0
